title: [feature] affectUI foundation: the 21 primitives stay byte-identical and alone, and every --aui- token they read is set from Spawn's theme roles for light and dark (styles/aui.css), with Spawn's radii by what reads them and text names at 4.5:1; no page changes
prompt:
Spawn, mission 4, objective 119 [feature]: affectUI's primitives wear Spawn's theme. This is the foundation of the affectUI series (the owner via lead-mac, 11-13 14:02): the affectUI files the owner landed get Spawn's look in both themes, with no page changed yet.

Where things stand. The owner's push a9cf34c1 put affectUI's 20 free primitives under web/src/components/ui/<name>.tsx, byte for byte, with web/src/components/ui/affectui.sha256 and the notice in web/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md. The lead's kit commit then puts the kit's -clean variant at six of those paths and adds kpi-chart.tsx (21 files). Nothing imports them. Each file injects its own styles and reads its colours, radii, shadows and fonts as `var(--aui-<name>, <affectUI's default>)`, in its light rules and in its dark rules (`:where(.dark,[data-theme=dark])`). Spawn's web/src/theme.ts already sets <html data-theme="dark"|"light">, which those dark rules match. 33 names are read; list them with `grep -oh -- '--aui-[a-z0-9-]*' web/src/components/ui/*.tsx | sort -u`. Nothing defines them today, so each primitive would wear affectUI's palette, not Spawn's.

The kit and its source (the owner, 11-13 15:00). The owner provided an affectUI component kit and decided: use its components as needed, the paid ones included, copied byte for byte into web/src/components/ui/ by the lead's owner push with a sha256 list. The kit's source stays inside the private repository: it is not published anywhere outside it, and no part of it is quoted in a sync note, a review, a contract or a notice. There is no notice line for the kit; the landed notice for the first 20 files stays as it is.

Required behaviour.
- The files in web/src/components/ui/ are third-party and are never edited, renamed or moved. That directory holds exactly the list the lead's kit commit lands (the 20 paths a9cf34c1 landed, six of them now holding the kit's -clean variant: badge, button, card, empty-state, skeleton and tooltip, and the new kpi-chart.tsx from the kit's -clean kpi-chart; segmented-control and the other 13 stay as landed: 21 files) and affectui.sha256: no index file and no wrapper goes in there. Spawn's own components/ui.tsx sits beside that directory, so "../ui" alone resolves to Spawn's file: always import a primitive by its full path (for example "../ui/button"; rev-g's note).
- Spawn's own stylesheet, web/src/styles/aui.css, imported by web/src/index.css after spawn.css, declares every `--aui-*` name the 21 files read. They are declared in a rule that applies under both [data-theme="light"] and [data-theme="dark"]. The values come from spawn.css's theme roles (surface, inset, line, ink-1..3, the accent and focus, the status inks and tints, the trace hues, the shadow ladder) and from index.css's font stacks. There is no literal colour, so both themes follow the roles.
- Text contrast. The primitives set some hue names as text, not only as tints: kpi-chart's delta (red, green), code-block's tokens (orange), segmented-control's active label (blue). A -mark or trace-* role is checked by scripts/contrast.mjs only at 3:1 (marks), and in the light theme several fall under 4.5:1. So every hue or status name the files may set as text takes a text role, which holds 4.5:1: red fail-ink, green ok-ink, orange wait-ink, blue accent-ink, teal info-ink, purple judge-ink; info, success, warning and danger the status inks; ink and muted ink and ink-2. Each of these names is at least 4.5:1 (WCAG 2.2 AA for text) on --aui-surface and on --aui-subtle, in both themes.
- Shape: Spawn's radii (spawn.css's @theme), by what reads each name: --aui-radius-sm, read by the chips (badge, kbd), is --radius-chip (6px); --aui-radius, read by the controls (button, select, segmented-control, toggle-group, pagination), is --radius-control (8px); --aui-radius-lg, read by cards and overlays (card, dialog, popover), is --radius-card (10px).
- Motion: aui.css adds none. Each primitive keeps its own prefers-reduced-motion rules, and Spawn's stay as they are.
- Spawn's wrappers and compositions will live outside that directory, in web/src/components/aui/. This objective adds none: the first page that uses a primitive (Home, 120) adds them, where a page shows them.
- No page changes here. App.tsx and every page and component of Spawn's stay as they are; the Home page is objective 120.

The approved dependency. The owner approved @hugeicons/core-free-icons at exactly 4.4.0 (icons only). The approved set is named in rsi/scenarios/web-dependencies-reviewed; package.json and the lockfile carry it from K2 on (the lead's next owner push); 119 imports no icon. At this objective's base, neither web/package.json nor web/pnpm-lock.yaml names it, and no file in web/src/components/ui/ imports it (badge and empty-state take icon data as a prop and only mention Hugeicons in a comment). So this objective adds no package and changes neither file; do not add a pin here, since that changes the set check-web.sh checks. rev-g's conditions hold for every later use: (C1) icons come only as constants imported at build time, never icon data from an API or from storage; (C2) named imports from the package, never `import *`.

What the fleet can show without a browser. tsc and the build pass (check-web runs them, and so does the scenario). There is no DOM test runner in web/ (node --test runs pure modules only), and adding one (jsdom, vitest, a browser) is a new dependency, which is the owner's to approve. So nothing here may need one. This objective adds no mapping logic in TypeScript, so it adds no web/test file; every existing web test still passes.

Files (expected; no other open objective touches them): web/src/styles/aui.css (new) and web/src/index.css (one @import line). About 70 lines (the throwaway: +61).

Acceptance: rsi/scenarios/119.sh. Black box over the tree under test (the working directory) and its build.
(1) web/src/components/ui/ holds exactly the 21 files, each with the sha256 the scenario carries itself (the owner's list; the tree's own affectui.sha256 is not trusted), and affectui.sha256. Nothing is changed and nothing is added.
(2) Every `--aui-*` name the 21 files read is declared in web/src/styles/aui.css, under both [data-theme="light"] and [data-theme="dark"]. Its value holds no literal colour, and each custom property it uses is declared by Spawn's own styles.
(3) `npm run build` (tsc, then vite) passes into a directory of the scenario's own, and the built CSS declares every one of those names.
(4) The radii: in each theme, --aui-radius-sm resolves to spawn.css's --radius-chip, --aui-radius to --radius-control, and --aui-radius-lg to --radius-card.
(5) Contrast: in each theme, each of --aui-ink, -muted, -info, -success, -warning, -danger, -blue, -orange, -teal, -red, -green and -purple, resolved through aui.css and Spawn's roles, is at least 4.5:1 on --aui-surface and on --aui-subtle, measured as Spawn's scripts/contrast.mjs measures (oklch to sRGB, WCAG relative luminance).

Verified by: the gate runs 119.sh on the candidate. After the landing, the lead runs check-web (tsc, the build, node --test) on the landed tree and posts the result. No page uses the tokens yet, so lead-mac's screenshot pair comes with the first page that does (120, Home, light and dark at 1400 px and at phone width), and it checks there that the primitives wear Spawn's palette and radii.
